subject: MSA + Order Form: Tier-shift addendum and coverage reconciliation
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@orchid.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Christopher Moon <c.moon@procurecorp.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal paperwork — our counters (addendum + Exhibit B)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the renewal packet and the breakout on seat tiers. We reviewed the MSA and order form with our procurement and legal teams and attached our redlines for the addendum (orchid_redline_v1.docx). Key asks from our side:

- Preserve the data-residency paragraph in Section 6 (we need EU data residency for a subset).
- Clarify the surge-burst definition in Exhibit B so it aligns to usage bands (we proposed a short table).
- Limit the SLA credit cap to 3 months for recurring outages; procurement flagged the current language as open-ended.

We want to keep term at 24 months but will consider a 12-month option if the surge definitions and residency language remain. Can you loop in legal and Ben for pricing confirmation?

Attachments: orchid_redline_v1.docx (redlines)

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Director, Procurement 
Orchid AI

Date: 2025-05-18T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork — our counters (addendum + Exhibit B)

Aisha — thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful notes. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Laura/Markus from Legal/Ops to scope the redlines and confirm signpath.

High-level response:
- Data residency: we can preserve a scoped EU residency carve for the named tenant(s) — Laura, can you confirm feasible Wording for Exhibit D?
- Surge definition: we like the proposed table; wanting to ensure it won't affect autoscaling behavior. Ben — do the proposed tiers change the committed throughput pricing materially?
- SLA credits: Redwood is willing to narrow the cap but we should keep a clear remediation path. Markus, I left a few inline comments in redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.docx (attached).

Next steps: Laura to provide legal wording by EOD tomorrow, Ben to share pricing impact, then we can exchange a final countersign doc. If Orchid is comfortable, we can start DocuSign on the limited changes and keep the 24-month term.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2025-05-18T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork — our counters (addendum + Exhibit B)

Rachel / team — quick notes from pricing/procurement:

- The table Aisha suggested (tiers + burst thresholds) is fine; however, if Orchid splits residency by tenant and applies a dedicated pool we need to re-evaluate committed capacity pricing (likely +8–12% for EU-isolated GPUs).
- For a 24mo commitment we can absorb 50% of the uplift for the first 12 months and then revert to standard list pricing — I flagged the numbers in the redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.docx.
- SLA credit cap: we'll accept a hard cap equal to the monthly committed spend (capped at 3 months) but need to preserve the remedy ladder (service credits then rollback option).

As an operations note: if they proceed with the EU carve we should propose a phased migration timeline (60–90 days) to avoid double-billing for replicated cache warm-up. I attached our procurement_playbook.pdf for the sequence (internal).

On the legal redlines, Laura/Markus — please prioritize the data-residency phrasing and the surge definition so we can produce a countersign by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2025-05-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork — our counters (addendum + Exhibit B)

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick alignment. We reviewed Ben's notes with our engineering and confirmed we can accept the +8% uplift on committed EU-isolated pool for the first 12 months under the phased migration plan. We also accept the SLA credit cap language as long as the remedy ladder remains intact.

Attached is Orchid's final countersign (orchid_final_countersign.pdf) with the updated residency callout preserved and the surge table integrated. Please confirm you have an internal signpath and whether you want us to start DocuSign or wait for your legal to sign first.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/embedded/signing/3fa1b2c9

If you can confirm by EOD we will route on our side.

Best,
Aisha Khan

Orchid AI
